what: F1 study A, written before any pull request is read for it: when a public AI-agent pull request moves a runtime or an image to a new version in a file, how often does the repository still pin the old version elsewhere at that pull request's head (a copy left behind, by itemator/leftbehind.py as merged in !458 and !460, frozen), and, for merged ones, was such a copy moved by a later commit or named by a reviewer? Read-only; GET only; nothing is posted anywhere.
dataset: The AIDev pull_request table on disk (data/pull_request.parquet, 33,596 rows: the popular-repository subset of hao-li/AIDev, CC-BY-4.0) for the frame; GitHub's REST API, GET only, authenticated as the user's read-only gh login, for files, trees and contents; data/pr_review_comments.parquet for review comments.
frame: Pull requests whose title, in lower case, matches FRAME_RE = \b(bump|bumps|update|updates|upgrade|upgrades|move|moves|pin|pins)\b.{0,80}\b(php|node|nodejs|node\.js|python|ruby|go|golang|java|jdk|openjdk|dotnet|alpine|debian|ubuntu|postgres|postgresql|mysql|mariadb|redis|nginx|image|base image|docker|dockerfile)\b. All matches, in id order; if there are more than 400, a sample of 400 drawn with random.Random(20261024).
move: For each pull request in the frame: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number} (base and head sha), GET .../pulls/{number}/files (all pages, at most 3000 files), and for each modified file that itemator.leftbehind.kind_of reads, its text at the base sha and the head sha (GET contents with ref). itemator.leftbehind.moved decides whether the pull request moves a pin. A pull request whose head sha or files cannot be read is 'unreadable', counted apart, never dropped.
scan: For each pull request with a move: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{head_sha}?recursive=1; every path itemator.leftbehind.find would read (kind_of, not skipped_path, at most MAX_FILES), read at the head sha; itemator.leftbehind.find with the listed versions taken from the title and body only when they name a CVE (as the CI job does). A truncated tree, or a read that fails, makes the pull request 'partly read', counted apart and reported.
unit: one pull request with a move
primary_outcome: The share of readable pull requests with a move for which find names at least one copy left behind, with counts and a Wilson 95% interval; also the number of copies, and of files, per such pull request.
secondary_outcomes: followed: for each merged pull request with a copy left behind, whether some commit on the base branch within 90 days after merged_at changed that copy's file so that the copy's pin reaches at least its target (GET .../commits?sha={base_ref}&path={file}&since&until, then the file at each such commit, oldest first). Reported as counts of copies and of pull requests; 'not followed' includes files changed in other ways.
named: whether a review comment on the same pull request (data/pr_review_comments.parquet) contains the left file's path or its file name.
still old: whether the copy's file at the base branch's tip today still holds a pin of that image or runtime below the target.
reading_rule: Report the primary share first, in plain words, with counts. Kill rule, fixed now: if the share is under 3% of readable pull requests with a move, the README calls the check narrow on real agent changes and says so in one sentence. A copy left behind is a fact about the files, not proof of a bug: a test of an old version, or a second image on purpose, are named the same way. 'Followed' says someone moved the copy later; it does not say the old copy caused harm. If fewer than 30 pull requests have a move, list them instead of a share.
limits: The frame is found from titles, so a version move with another title is missed, and a title that matches may move no pin. AIDev covers popular public repositories on GitHub. Pins are read by fixed rules from files; a build argument or CI variable that overrides a version is not seen (docs/limits.md). The head tree is read as it stood at the pull request's head, not at its merge. One run of frozen rules; nothing is tuned on these pull requests.
seen_before_registration: Nothing from this frame. The patch-day replay (results/patchday_replay_v1.json) read the 19 AIDev pull requests that name a CVE and found 15 with no version-only file. leftbehind.py was written against hand-made repositories in tests/test_leftbehind.py and the staged second-project merge request !20 (2026-10-24).
